title: perf(canary): add automated latency/throughput regression + ML drift detector with rollout guards
author: Priya Menon
summary: Adds an automated detector for latency/throughput regressions and ML-based distribution drift scoring into the perf-canary pipeline and wiring rollout guard actions (traffic hold, rollback, notify).
description:
Motivation: Our existing perf canary rules are threshold-based and brittle across workloads. This change adds a lightweight ML-based drift detector for latency and throughput distributions, integrates it into the canary evaluation pipeline, and implements rollout guards (traffic hold, auto-rollback, canary cooldown/hysteresis) to reduce noisy rollouts and improve safety during deployments.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds 'drift_score' and 'anomaly_score' calculation to the perf-canary service using recent-window distribution comparisons (14-day baseline by default).
- Computes multi-signal evaluation: p50/p95/p99 latency histograms + request TPS, KV cache hit-rate as a covariate, and error-rate.
- Adds hysteresis and sensitivity tuning per-customer and per-model; default policy uses adaptive thresholds to reduce false positives.
- Extends rollout guards to support: hold traffic, step-back (rollback), notify on-call, and automatic retry after cooldown.
- Adds APIs and console wiring for viewing drift scores and for manual override of rollout guards.
- Includes unit + integration tests and a small load test harness used in our CI perf job.

Implementation notes:
- Detector implementation is in perf-canary/service/drift_detector.py and uses a lightweight KL-divergence + EWMA-based anomaly score to keep compute low on control-plane pods. We avoid heavy models so this can run as part of the canary evaluation step.
- Baseline windows and sensitivity are configurable via perf-canary config and Helm values (deployment/helm/perf-canary-values.yaml).
- The canary evaluation pipeline now computes both deterministic threshold checks and drift_score; the final decision uses a combined rule with configurable weights so teams can opt into ML signals gradually.
- Rollout guards were refactored into a small rule engine (perf-canary/service/guard_engine.go) supporting actions (hold, rollback, partial-scale-back, notify).

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests added for detector math and guard logic (perf-canary/tests/unit/*).
- Integration test added that runs the canary evaluation loop against synthetic latency distributions to validate detection sensitivity and auto-rollback behavior (perf-canary/tests/integration/test_auto_rollback.py).
- CI has a perf-canary-load-tests job that runs a short synthetic load profile; results attached in the PR checks.
- Local load benches were run against a staging pool with seeded regressions to tune defaults.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy to staging perf-canary (canary namespace) and enable ML detection for a small subset of teams (opt-in).
2) Run for 48h and monitor false-positive rate and on-call alerts.
3) Gradually ramp to 10% traffic gating for new rollouts, then 50% after 7 days, then 100% if no issues.
4) Provide a toggle in Console to disable ML-signal or tune sensitivity per team.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Load test job added to CI
- [x] Docs: perf-canary documentation updated with detector description and config examples
- [x] Helm values added for config

Related: ENG-3421 (canary reliability), SRE-112 (auto-rollback during incidents).

Notes: This PR focuses on safety and low compute overhead to avoid adding cost to the control plane. We left further work (per-model learned baselines and supervised regressors) to follow-ups.

review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Nice approach. Concern: KL-divergence will be sensitive to histogram binning and low-volume models. Please add a guard for low-sample windows and document expected false-positive rate.

Author (Priya Menon): Added low-sample guard (minimum 500 samples window) and per-tenant opt-out. Updated docs and helm values. See commit 'ci(tests): add integration test for auto-rollback on regression'.
Maya Chen: Can we emit granular metrics for the drift scoring pipeline (raw KL, EWMA, weighting) so SREs can build alerts? Also request e2e test verifying rollback triggers in the canary pipeline.
Author (Priya Menon): Emitted metrics: perf_canary.drift.kl, perf_canary.drift.ewma, perf_canary.drift.score. Added integration test that simulates step regression to validate rollback.

Luca Romano: Verified load test results in CI and validated that default sensitivity produced <2% FP in staging. Approving with one optional comment about exposing a Debug UI for the scoring histograms.

release_notes: Added ML-based drift detection to perf-canary with rollout guards: adaptive thresholds, per-tenant opt-out, metrics emitted for drift scoring, and automatic hold/rollback actions. Default settings are conservative; operators can tune sensitivity via Helm values.
